fixes.explanation: Traditions sound respectable, friend, but that isn't the word here. God says these prophets prophesy “…out of their own imagination…” (Ezekiel 13:2). The words came from their own imagination. Even a smudged recipe card has more behind it than that.

Scrolls would at least mean somebody wrote something down! But God never mentions a scroll in this verse. He says they prophesy “…out of their own imagination…” (Ezekiel 13:2). The source is their own imagination.

Not quite, baker. God says the opposite: “You did not go up to the gaps or restore the wall around the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 13:5). They did not go up to the gaps, and they did not restore the wall.

False, and God says it plainly. “You did not go up to the gaps or restore the wall around the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 13:5). They did not go up to the gaps, and they did not restore the wall. All talk, no trowel.

That's the one. God says the wall needed restoring “…so that it would stand in the battle on the Day of the LORD.” (Ezekiel 13:5). It had a job to do on that day. And God says these prophets did not restore it.

A famine isn't what this verse says, friend. God says the wall needed restoring so it would stand “…in the battle on the Day of the LORD.” (Ezekiel 13:5). A battle, not a famine. A wall is built for the day somebody pushes against it.

I get the guess, friend, but this verse says something else. God says the wall needed restoring “…so that it would stand in the battle on the Day of the LORD.” (Ezekiel 13:5). Nothing here about a homecoming. It's about a wall holding up in battle.

Yep. The LORD did not send them, “yet they wait for the fulfillment of their message.” (Ezekiel 13:6). They hand out the message and then stand around expecting it to come true. I think that takes some nerve. It's like never turning the oven on and then waiting for the cookies to come out.

That would be a nice twist, baker, but it isn't what the verse says. They claim, “Thus declares the LORD…” when the LORD did not send them (Ezekiel 13:6). Instead, God says “…they wait for the fulfillment of their message.”
Peace, baker. God says they led His people astray, “…saying, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace…” (Ezekiel 13:10). One soothing word, and there was no peace behind it.

Repent would be a different word entirely, friend. Repent isn't the word in this verse. God says these prophets led His people astray “…saying, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace…” (Ezekiel 13:10). The word they gave was peace.

Guarding a wall is real work, friend, and that's not what these prophets are doing. God says they were “…whitewashing any flimsy wall that is built…” (Ezekiel 13:10). They were whitewashing it, not guarding it.

Other way around, baker. God tells Ezekiel, “…tell those whitewashing the wall that it will fall.” (Ezekiel 13:11). Rain will come in torrents, hailstones will plunge down, and a windstorm will burst forth. That wall isn't standing.

Not quite, friend. After the storm, God says He will tell them, “The wall is gone, and so are those who whitewashed it…” (Ezekiel 13:15). That comes after He has vented His wrath against the wall and against those who whitewashed it. The wall is gone, and so are they.

False. God says, “The wall is gone, and so are those who whitewashed it…” (Ezekiel 13:15). He names them as the prophets of Israel who saw a vision of peace for Jerusalem when there was no peace. The wall and the whitewashers are both gone.

False. God tells His prophet to set his face against these women and says, “Prophesy against them” (Ezekiel 13:17). So he has something to say to them. It starts with “Woe to the women who sew magic charms on their wrists…” (Ezekiel 13:18).

True, and it's a hard line. God says that by lying to My people who would listen, “…you have killed those who should not have died and spared those who should not have lived.” (Ezekiel 13:19). Their lies pointed life and death the wrong way. I think this one hurts.

It's true, baker. God says, “…you have killed those who should not have died and spared those who should not have lived.” (Ezekiel 13:19). That came from lying to His people who would listen. I think this verse is hard to hear.

Judgment is in this chapter, friend, but that's not what God says here about these souls. God says, “So I will free the souls you have ensnared like birds.” (Ezekiel 13:20). The trapped ones are the ones He frees.

Wicked goes in the second blank. God says they “…encouraged the wicked not to turn from their evil ways to save their lives…” (Ezekiel 13:22). So the lies disheartened the righteous and encouraged the wicked to keep to their evil ways.
Exiles isn't a word this verse uses, friend. God says these women disheartened “the righteous” and encouraged “the wicked” (Ezekiel 13:22). Those are the two words that fit the blanks.
Elders isn't a word this verse uses, baker. God says they disheartened “the righteous” and encouraged “the wicked” (Ezekiel 13:22). The blanks are for those two.
